messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: multiple containers on paged-attn fleet showing progressive resident memory growth -> OOM + CUDA driver resets. Aggregated error rate across region: 6.8%. Auto-escalation to incidents channel.

maria: acknowledging, jumping in. which pool?

incident-bot: affected pool: rwd-paged-attn-eu-west-2-[redwood-serving-allocs], nodes: 6/48 reporting OOMs, 4 node restarts in last 12m. Top error signatures: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS, CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED, kernel panic -> container crash.

alex: seeing the same in dashboards. KV cache free % trending down even for low qps. suspect fragmentation + slow leak in slab allocator after attention page churn.

sam: @maria can you confirm customer impact? CS bot, ping.

customer-success-bot: Customer telemetry: 12 tenants impacted; 3 tenants hit >10% 5xx on generation endpoint; avg latency spiked 2-3x for affected requests. No billing anomalies yet.

maria: ok. immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause canary/batch-heavy routes into paged-attn pool 2) enable fallback routing to non-paged-attn model variant 3) drain and reprovision flagged nodes 4) collect a memory profile before restart. I'll take 1 & 2.

alex: doing step 2 now: updating smart-routing policy to route model:rw-paged-v1 -> rw-nopage-v1 for tier=prod in eu-west-2. Command:

```bash
redwood-cli route update --region eu-west-2 --from-model rw-paged-v1 --to-model rw-nopage-v1 --filter "tier:prod" --dry-run=false
```

alex: routing change pushed. traffic shift at ~1715010300. watching error metrics.

sam: starting drains on nodes: rwd-node-12, rwd-node-17 (most OOMs). running:

```bash
kubectl cordon rwd-node-12 || true
kubectl drain rwd-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60
```

sam: collecting coredump from one container before kill. log snippet:

```
[2024-09-08T21:02:11Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 23812 (rw-infer) total-vm: 3244320kB, anon-rss: 2890220kB
2024-09-08T21:02:13Z rw-infer[23812]: cuda: CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED at aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Blas.cpp:142
2024-09-08T21:02:13Z rw-infer[23812]: alloc: requested page_id=12345678 size=64k but slab free fragments: 0
```

sam: uploading core + jemalloc stats to /mnt/incidents/1715009999/ for postmortem.

maria: temporary patch: reduce paged-attn eviction_threshold to aggressively evict small fragments, and enable immediate kv-slab-defrag on low-mem events. Alex, can you apply policy change?

alex: applying:

```json
{"kv_paged": {"evict_threshold_pct": 3, "aggressive_defrag": true, "defrag_window_s": 30}}
```

alex: config pushed to config-service at 1715010605. Rolling to pool.

maria: monitor for regressions. If OOMs persist after drains+defrag, we'll revert paged-attn and schedule hotfix rollback.

incident-bot: metric update: post-route-change error rate down to 3.2% at 1715011000. Node restarts reduced.

sam: note: one node flapped due to driver reset during coredump collection; raising ticket to infra about driver/ubuntu kernel combo on rwd-node-17.

alex: confirmed memory growth flattened on 4/6 nodes after aggressive defrag. two nodes still show slow leak (slope ~ +1.1MB/min). coredumps from those nodes show repeated allocations for KV cache page metadata. suspect leak in page metadata update path when attention pages are retired with concurrent requests.

maria: ok assign owners: alex -> temporary routing + config; sam -> node drains + core collection; maria -> customer comms & incident lead. escalation: eng-runtime on standby (pinged).

eng-oncall: standing by. will triage reproducer on a small repro harness. request: collect heap profiles (jeprof) and run with ASAN builds if possible.

sam: captured heap snapshot and jemalloc hist in /mnt/incidents/1715009999/hist-1715010800.tar.gz. Also saved container env:

```
MODEL=rw-paged-v1
SEQUENCE_LEN=4096
BATCHING=continuous
PAGE_SIZE=64k
KV_SLAB_COUNT=16384
```

maria: customer comms draft (for CS):

"We observed intermittent memory growth on our paged-attention allocator which caused container restarts and transient increased 5xx rates for a subset of requests in eu-west-2. We've mitigated by routing impacted traffic to a non-paged-attention variant and applying aggressive defragmentation to reduce resident set size. We're continuing to investigate root cause and will follow up with a postmortem and timeline."

customer-success-bot: Sent to affected tenants at 1715011500. No immediate escalations.

incident-bot: update: at 1715012100, aggregate error rate back down to baseline (0.8%). All drained nodes are now reprovisioned except rwd-node-17 which is quarantined for kernel/driver analysis.

maria: next steps: 1) eng-runtime to produce repro and patch - likely a metadata leak in page retirement path. 2) schedule canary with patched allocator at low traffic 3) add extra metrics: page_meta_count, retire_queue_len, slab_frag_ratio. 4) follow-up postmortem. Who can take the bug?

alex: I'll take the bug. creating internal issue: RW-4567 "paged-attn page_meta leak during retirement under concurrency". attaching heap snapshots + logs.

sam: adding runbook note: when OOM signature shows \"alloc: requested page_id... slab free fragments:0\" then: - immediate routing fallback - aggressive defrag - drain nodes - collect coredump & jemalloc stats - quarantine node.

maria: closing active incident channel for now. if anyone sees new OOMs, reopen. Great job keeping customer impact limited. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated. Retain logs and artifacts at s3://redwood-incidents/1715009999/.
